result.title: The Frontier Must Grow - Self-proposed, interpreter-labelled training roughly doubles a 4B model's accuracy on a fresh exam as its verified frontier grows
result.summary: A model can learn from problems it poses itself when an executable oracle supplies the answers. Qwen3-4B proposed Lua 5.1 programs; those it predicted wrong at least once in four samples joined a pool labelled by the interpreter, each round adding twice as many programs as the last (300, 900, 2100 in total), and each round trained a fresh adapter from the base on the pool. On the original exam the procedure met its registered criterion, an item-level test of each adapter against its predecessor. On a 2340-item exam drawn afterwards, accuracy rose from 8.3% to 16.7%; that follow-up's registered criteria were not met because round 1 gained nothing, while rounds 2 and 3 added 5.0 and 2.9 points on average, both intervals above zero. One fit on the same amount of base-proposed frontier data reached 14.6%, so the rounds' 2.1-point advantage is inconclusive. Three earlier registered series met no per-lineage criterion, and the same loop showed no gain on repository tasks or for a 27B agent in those configurations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文让 Qwen3-4B 自我提出 Lua 程序题，由解释器提供可执行答案构成逐轮倍增的题目池，每轮从基座重训适配器，检验这种「验证前沿」增长能否提升新考试准确率；随访集上准确率由 8.3% 升至 16.7%，但注册判据未全满足，同等数据单次拟合达 14.6% 使轮次优势不确定，另有仓库任务与 27B 设定下的负结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 自提议数据加可执行验证器标注、逐轮扩池并从基座重训的做法，可能为 LVR 中缺少中间状态标签时的轨迹自生成、验证信号使用与轮次贡献核查提供参照线索；但属代码文本任务且结果不稳，是否可迁移仍需核查原文。
